correctness.rationale: Scalar resolvent coefficients directly give the unique all-center calibration. Strict contraction supplies a unique invariant law; centered independent affine updates give V and geometric lag covariance, and geometric summation gives the exact sample-average limit. Two- and three-component rational identities factor into a square and a polynomial times r-1, respectively. Ten symbolic identity groups, 275 exact rational test cases and three seeded stochastic comparisons passed using the embedded verifier; these tests supplement, not replace, the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General iid random affine recursions subsume the basic covariance recurrence, and that elementary ingredient is expressly acknowledged. The identified broad proximal and estimator theorems do not directly imply the specific all-center distribution choice plus the exact two-component obstruction and three-component strict reverse sign; those are obtained by coefficient matching and special rational derivatives. A more comprehensive specialized theorem could still imply them and remains a priority risk.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary papers on stochastic proximal updates, generalized random resolvents, implicit SGD and proximal averages do not establish the precise conditional equality to the original sum together with the minimal component-count derivative-sign reversal. The basic affine-recursion moment formulas and convex-combination proximal-average facts are not claimed new. Named possible stronger equivalences and priority uncertainty are explicitly recorded.
residual_risks: A generic iid affine-recursion theorem could imply the covariance formulas, though not a demonstrated exact calibrated sampling law and minimal-component sign transition.
A specialized weighted quadratic resolvent or proximal-average publication may establish an equivalent choice or stronger statement not uncovered by the bounded searches.
The priority assessment is based on accessible records and selected relevant full-text sections, not an exhaustive universe of papers.

value.rationale: The exact curvature-calibrated sampling scheme removes conditional mean resolvent bias without a control-vector correction. Its stationary time-averaging precision is not monotone in the same direction across component structures: all two-component models forbid decreasing long-run variance, yet a stable natural three-component family has strict decrease despite rising iterate variance. This algebraic phase distinction has interpretive value for step-size design and independent proximal sampling.
